newsitem.title: UK: UK's Cambridge University gets $4 million gift.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cambridge University gets $4 million gift.

text.p: Britain's Cambridge University said on Monday a charitable foundation had given it 2.5 million pounds ($4.1 million) to aid its research into the cosmos.
The gift from the Maerit and Hans Rausing Charitable Foundation would go towards building a new centre for mathematical studies, the university said.
It said the charity's patron, Swedish professor Hans Rausing, was particularly fascinated by the study of the universe.

"Cambridge is the world leader in study of theoretical cosmology, and this tremendous support will help to strengthen our research and open up immensely exciting opportunities in this field," said Professor David Crighton, head of the department of applied mathematics and theoretical physics.

The university said it had a great tradition of cosmological research, and famous wheelchair-bound physicist Stephen Hawking currently occupies the Lucasian Chair in theoretical physics once held by Sir Isaac Newton.
